#: Scrub manifest for the nix collector. Its interface is a TREE — the profile link farm and the handful of small files inside each system closure — so its payloads are the filesystem transcribed (DESIGN, adjudication queue, 2026-08-19): read.json is every file the walk opened, listdir.json every directory it enumerated, realpath.json every link it resolved to a final target, readlink.json every link's own immediate target, mtime.json each profile link's creation time, and exists.json the presence questions the walk asked. Each is keyed the way a filesystem is — the directory, then the name inside it.
#scoping: Four of the six payloads are exactly one container and one member deep, so they all want the pattern '*.*' and a JSON object holds a key once. Every entry here therefore carries the payload-prefix scope ('realpath:*.*'), which exists for this case; without it three of the four would be classifiable by nothing and the run would refuse the variant outright.
#store_paths_are_nothing_and_that_is_a_c: Almost every key and value here is a /nix/store path. A store path is a BUILD hash over a derivation's inputs — public, reproducible, and identical on every machine that builds the same closure from the same nixpkgs — so it identifies a build and never a machine. That is why these are `nothing` rather than `identity`, and it is also why substituting them would be actively WRONG: the hash is exactly what makes two hosts' generations comparable, and a scrubbed one would teach a reader that two identical closures are two different ones.
#the_one_identifying_token_inside_a_stor: A system closure is named `nixos-system-<hostname>-<version>`, so the host's OWN name sits inside the path. No pattern here scrubs it, because it is not a field — it is a substring of a value whose other half must survive — and the tool's mechanism for an operator-chosen word inside free text is the run's --hostnames pass, exactly as it is for a libvirt domain name. ON THIS CAPTURE it did not need to fire: the guest carries nixpkgs' default hostname, the literal string `nixos`, which discloses nothing about any estate and could not be substituted anyway without mangling `nixos-version`, `nixos-system` and the distribution's own vocabulary. A re-stage on a host with a real hostname MUST pass it through --hostnames, and this paragraph is the only thing that says so.
#nixos_version_is_a_release_not_a_machin: nixos-version is the closure's record of which nixpkgs built it, the same string on every host running that release. configuration-revision and se-generation.json are the other half: a VCS revision and a build manifest naming the repository that builds the estate, which is estate-authored content whatever it happens to be on this guest — both are empty here because nothing wrote them, and classifying by what a capture happens to contain is how a manifest comes to be wrong on the next host.
#mtime_is_a_measurement: A profile link's mtime is when that generation was activated: a measurement of an event, not a property of a machine, and already published verbatim as the Created fact.
#member_keys: Every payload's second level is keyed by a FILENAME — nixos-version, kernel, system-2-link, specialisation — so each needs its own '*.~key' beside the container one. They are the names nix and nixpkgs give their own files, identical on every host, with one thing in them that varies: a profile link carries its generation NUMBER, which is a counter of how many times this machine has been rebuilt and not an identifier of it.
